item.title: Comfort Workshop
item.description:
The brief

Comfort Workshop is a made-to-measure furniture manufacturer where the buying decision is personal, considered and rarely completed in a single click. They needed more than a brochure site: they needed a digital platform that could build trust in public and help the team run the whole customer and production journey behind the scenes.

Website: comfortworkshop.co.uk · Brand: orange Squash-style wordmark

The public experience

The website is designed to educate, reassure and generate the right enquiries rather than push people through a standard online checkout. Customers can explore collections, fabrics and options, read useful guidance, request a brochure, book a home demonstration, arrange a showroom visit or contact the team directly.

item.title: Rennix Automotive
item.description:
The brief

Rennix does meticulous work for cars people care about. The old digital presence did not carry the same confidence, craft or clarity.

The useful bit

We gave the business a visual language with some engineering in its bones: direct type, measured detail and a service journey that helps a visitor understand the standard of work before they pick up the phone.

The result

A specialist local presence that feels precise without feeling closed-off.

item.title: Riser Recliner Directory
item.description:
The brief

The Riser Recliner Directory started with a simple question: how do you help someone compare an important, highly personal purchase without adding more noise?

The useful bit

We designed a structured search experience around the questions people can answer — room, support, fit, budget and need — and built a content model that makes the information useful to people and discoverable in search.

The result

A directory that behaves less like a list and more like a helpful guide.

item.title: The Fox at Kirton
item.description:
The brief

The Fox at Kirton needed a website with enough warmth and appetite to do the pub justice, while making the practical things — food, rooms and bookings — easy to find.

The useful bit

We built a flexible content system around the rhythm of the place: menus can change, events can have their moment and a hungry visitor can book without detouring through three other sites.

The result

One lively digital home for the whole experience.

item.title: The Specialist Seating Company
item.description:
The brief

When the product range is technical and the decision is personal, a catalogue can quickly become a wall of information. The Specialist Seating Company needed a clearer way to help different audiences find confidence.

The useful bit

We reorganised the website around needs and outcomes rather than internal product categories. Quote requests now carry the context the team needs, so the first human conversation can start with advice instead of data collection.
